messages:
maria: FYI support just escalated a Dedicated customer (axiom-health) — huge throughput drop starting ~03:12 UTC. RPS down ~60%, tail latency spikes, some 429s and 504s. They say requests still billed but responses are painfully slow.
jen: seen the thread. They attached a small log dump and a short replay trace. sending here. cc @rahul @tao
jen: log snippet they sent:
```
2026-03-17T03:12:05Z batcher.INFO formed_batch size=1 tokens=4 tenant=axiom-health
2026-03-17T03:12:05Z kvcache.WARN miss tenant=axiom-health key=conv:123
2026-03-17T03:12:05Z scheduler.DEBUG window_drain_oscillation tenant=axiom-health target_tokens=512 current_window_ms=50
2026-03-17T03:12:06Z request.ERROR id=abc123 status=504 downstream_timeout
2026-03-17T03:12:07Z autoscaler.INFO scale_down candidate=pod-47 reason=idle_check fail_count=3
```
maria: notable: a lot of "formed_batch size=1" lines. looks like the continuous batcher is flushing tiny batches instead of coalescing.
rahul: did they change per-tenant config recently? max_batch_tokens or window_ms?
jen: they applied a global profile tweak on Mar 16: set continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens=1024 for higher throughput (was 512). also increased window_ms to 50 to favor larger batches.
tao: that combination can backfire with streaming responses. if a single request starts streaming tokens back, the batcher target can get fragmented and end up draining repeatedly, forming single-request batches. essentially the batcher waits for token budget then flushes small batches when a stream yields token. explains the 1-size batches.
josh: also seeing autoscaler chatter in the logs — scale_down candidate then quick scale_up. oscillation could be reducing effective capacity right when bursts happen -> noisy neighbor effect.
rahul: action items to test: 1) repro with controlled replay; 2) toggles to try in prod as short mitigations: lower max_batch_tokens and lower window_ms, enable dynamic_batching=true; 3) pin tenant to an isolated pool if noisy neighbor suspected.
maria: can someone run a replay? jen, you have the customer's replay id?
jen: replay id: replay-20260317-axh-57. run like: `./tools/replay --id replay-20260317-axh-57 --target=dedicated-us-west --rate=40`
tao: I'll run a canary replay against a staging pool with current prod config to reproduce. then I'll apply a mitigation on a single dedicated host: patch continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens=400 and continuous_batcher.window_ms=8 and re-run.
rahul: if that fixes, we'll roll the change account-wide for axiom-health and then evaluate default profile. also add a short cooldown on autoscaler (autoscaler.cooldown_seconds -> 90s) to avoid oscillation.
jen: customer is sensitive — we should also enable per-tenant circuit breaker to return earlier 429s instead of long tails while we debug. set tenant.rate_limit_mode=fail_fast for axiom-health.
maria: any quick commands to patch tenant config?
tao: patch via control plane: 
```bash
curl -X PATCH "https://control.redwood/api/v1/tenants/axiom-health/config" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"continuous_batcher": {"max_batch_tokens": 400, "window_ms": 8}, "rate_limit_mode":"fail_fast"}'
```
josh: I'll also pin axiom-health to pool `dedicated-us-west-axh` and give it extra weight while we sort noisy neighbor issues.
ops-bot: deploy-batcher-config STARTED by tao on pool staging-dedicated at 03:45 UTC
tao: can reproduce in staging: with prod profile I see the same 1-size batch formation and throughput drop. after patch -> batches coalesced (mean batch size x6) and tail latency dropped ~55%.
jen: reported back to customer with ETA for mitigation. want to make change on prod in ~10m window, low-traffic period.
rahul: next steps:
- tao: apply prod tenant patch and monitor for 30m (owner)
- josh: pin tenant to isolated pool and increase weight (owner)
- maria: coordinate customer comms and confirm billing behavior (owner)
- jen: enable debug traces for batcher for 2 hours and collect metrics
- ops-bot: open follow-up RFC to re-evaluate default continuous_batcher defaults and autoscaler cooldowns
jen: one more note — check prefix/KV cache eviction thresholds. logs show kvcache.WARN; if cache keeps missing, extra seq decoding can increase latency even with fixed batch sizes.
maria: agreed. thanks everyone. will update thread after prod patch. :thumbsup:
